newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FX cross midpoints could be base for EMU rates fix.
newsitem.headline: FX cross midpoints could be base for EMU rates fix.

text.p: Historical currency cross midpoints could form the basis for how exchange rates are pegged at the start of European economic and monetary union (EMU), Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Tuesday.

"A rigid interpretation of the (Maastricht) Treaty would say that the conversion rates must be based on the spot rates on December 31, 1998...but market rates could diverge significantly from the rates that are desirable from an economic point of view," Maystadt told a business forum in Arlon, Belgium.
A copy of the speech was released by the finance ministry.

European Union finance ministers have often expressed fears about foreign exchange instability between the time EU leaders announce, at the beginning of 1998, which countries will participate in EMU, and January 1, 1999, when exchange rates are locked.
They fear the market could openly speculate against or seek to influence the rates used for EMU.
Several have suggested that to minimise this risk the bloc should announce in advance that currencies will be locked at an average exchange rate calculated using several months or years data.
Maystadt said that currency pair midpoints over a two-year period prior to January 1, 1999, could also form the basis for the decision at which exchange rates are locked.

"In effect, if the conversion rates , or the method that will be used to fix them, are pre-announced, the market should normally converge towards the chosen rates or that which equate to the method announced," Maystadt said.
Maystadt reiterated that finance ministers have already decided that the conversion rates chosen will extend to six figures.
